pin_row_note: headpin-column base row read on stack_349_351 (lowest visible base 555.7 at f349, ~556 at f350); ball centre 555 at f349 vs 557.5 at f348. The ball BOTTOM (y+r) reaches the headpin base row only at f354 (549.5 vs 550.1).
method: Every path point is a hand read from 3x gridded ball crops (gc_<f>.jpg) and lane-width crops with row brightness/|dx| profiles at the ball row (combo_/lane_<f>.jpg), plus tall 5x panels of each lane edge over rows ~515-610 for f342-357 (edge_L*/edge_R*.jpg), all on the SOURCE video decoded sequentially; board = 1 + 38*(x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x) with both edges read in the same frame at the ball centre row (board_contact repeats it at about y+r). Entry board is the median of edge-profile reads at pin_hit-1..+1, a pin-column ruler at four frames (headpin column = lowest base; 6 in column stagger = 5.49 units in this 38-unit convention) and a ball-diameter ruler (17 px = 7.8 units) at three frames.
limits: release+6 (f303) is inside the ball-invisible span 299-306, so the path starts at f307 (motion-blurred ball, r 29 from the blur extent). The left gutter runs into the image border at f321-335 (left_x 6-46), so those left edges are +-5 px; near the deck the left edge is a blurred diagonal and reads +-3-4 px, the right edge +-2-3 px, which is +-0.8-1.3 boards per path point at the far end (e.g. f352 reads 11.3 between 9.5 at f350 and 9.7 at f354). The pin rack is narrower than the edges: the 7 pin columns span 65 px against 92-95 px edge to edge (expected 36 in / 41.5 in = 0.87, seen 0.70), the same disagreement loop 1 found; pin ruler and edges still agree within ~1 board here because the ball is near the right edge. The task text's pin map (7-pin 33, 10-pin 7, 3 units per column) was NOT used: it disagrees with its own 7.8-unit ball scale; with it the pin reads would be about 2-3 boards higher. Ball radius at the deck is 8-9 px +-1, so the ball ruler is +-10-15 % in scale (f356 ball ruler 13.2 is the outlier). pin_row_frame uses the ball centre; at the far end the centre is ~r above the contact point, so the ball reaches the pin-base row with its contact point only at ~f354. Camera is handheld and pans ~3-5 px/frame at the end, so nothing is carried between frames.

pin_row.note_prev: NOT re-derived; kept 349 / contact row 354 from the existing truth, flagged. On zoom_352_363_215_538.jpg the ball is still in front of the standing rack at f352-358, is first overlapped by front pins at f359-360, and the first pin moves at f370, 14 frames after the cut pin_hit 356. The base row 556 is probably the bottom of the deck reflection, as on 191913 and 191253: a pin-height base (auto pin top 497 at f360 + 34 px + 3.5) gives ~542 at f356, which moves the centre crossing to f352 and the contact row to f356, and 2D overlap starts around f359-360 (not occlusion; use est_60ft_frame_from_contact). pin_row.method: pin-height base: headpin-column pin top (head top, not the neck stripe) + 15 in x lane px/in at the base row + 3.5 px (topmost white is the 5-pin, 20.8 in behind), per frame where detected within 6 px of the camera-compensated top, else compensated top + measured camera dy; ball centre from the path or a tracked purple component, r = geometric radius scaled by lane width; frame_contact_row = first frame with (y + r) - base <= +1 px.
pin_row.est_60ft_note: contact_frame - k, k=1 = rack row of the first pin within 6.1 units of the ball's board (about 1 frame per row); first visible pin motion lags the touch, so this is an upper bound

contact_note: Pins upright through f369 with the ball among them (zoom_364_375_210_522.jpg); first lean of the pins left of the ball at f370, pins flying f372. Aligned change 5.6 (f368) -> 9.8 (f369) -> 10.1 (f370) -> 14.7 (f371). +-1. This is 14 frames after the cut pin_hit 356.

exit.deflection: came in right of the headpin (board ~11), went through the rack drifting left about 7 boards and left the deck behind the headpin/5-pin line

exit_method: Ball read by eye on 5x camera-followed gridded crops (zoom_364_375_210_522.jpg) and matched to a compact moving purple component (a second component at x ~243 compensated is static and was ignored); lane edges are the wood-to-gutter Sobel step on rows 500-543 in front of the deck in the exit frame itself (rms 0.27-0.47 px), evaluated at the ball row.
exit_limits: Edge lines are extrapolated 55-95 px up to the ball row. The camera starts to whip at f373-376 (phase-correlation shifts jump 101 / 99 / 112 / 25 px), so the registered pin-ruler read (20.8) is unreliable and the ball cannot be followed after f375; exit frame is a lower bound if the ball stayed on the deck into the whip. Ball x +-2 px (~1 board) behind flying pins at f375.
